question: Does it still count as stealing if I didn't make a penny out of it and got nothing for myself?
note: Theft Act s.1: basic definition of theft, and it is immaterial whether the appropriation was for gain or for the thief's own benefit.

question: I was sure my mate wouldn't have minded me taking it. Can I still be done for stealing?
note: Theft Act s.2: when conduct is not to be regarded as dishonest, including belief in a right to the property or belief the owner would have consented.

question: I found a phone in the street and kept using it for a month. At what point does hanging onto it turn into a crime?
note: Theft Act s.3: assumption of an owner's rights, including a later assumption by someone who came by the item innocently.

question: Is it illegal to pick blackberries and wild mushrooms from a hedge if I'm going to sell them at a market stall?
note: Theft Act s.4: what can be owned for these purposes, covering land, wild plants picked for sale, and wild creatures.

question: The shop handed me way too much change and I walked off with it. Where do I stand?
note: Theft Act s.5: when something is treated as still belonging to someone else, including money handed over by mistake that you are obliged to give back.

question: I always meant to give the thing back eventually. Can they still say I meant to keep it for good?
note: Theft Act s.6: when treating something as your own to dispose of, or a long borrowing, counts as intending permanent deprivation.

question: How long can someone actually be sent down for if the jury finds them guilty of nicking stuff?
note: Theft Act s.7: maximum sentence on indictment for theft is seven years.

question: Some bloke shoved me into a wall and ran off with my phone. Is that treated more seriously than ordinary nicking?
note: Theft Act s.8: robbery, where force is used or threatened immediately before or at the time of stealing, punishable by life.

question: If someone climbs in through a window purely to smash the place up and doesn't take anything, what are they charged with?
note: Theft Act s.9: burglary, including entering as a trespasser intending to do unlawful damage to the building or its contents.

question: Does having a knife in your pocket while breaking into a house make things a lot worse for you?
note: Theft Act s.10: aggravated burglary, where the person has a firearm, imitation firearm, weapon of offence or explosive with them.

question: What happens if you walk out of a museum with something off the display during opening hours?
note: Theft Act s.11: removing articles from buildings open to the public to view, or from their grounds, carrying up to five years.

question: My neighbour took my bike for a spin round the block without asking and brought it back. Is that anything the police would care about?
note: Theft Act s.12: taking a conveyance without the owner's consent, with a separate lesser offence covering pedal cycles.

question: Someone drove off in a car that wasn't theirs and then wrote it off into a lamp post. Is that worse than just taking it?
note: Theft Act s.12A: aggravated vehicle-taking, where after the taking the vehicle is driven dangerously or injury or damage results.

question: My neighbour has been running an extension lead off my supply for months. Is that a criminal offence or just a billing dispute?
note: Theft Act s.13: dishonestly using, wasting or diverting electricity without authority, up to five years.

question: A parcel was lifted from a mail van somewhere between Glasgow and Belfast. Can they still be put in front of a court down here?
note: Theft Act s.14: extends jurisdiction to thefts and robberies involving mail bags or postal packets moving between jurisdictions in the British postal area.

question: My boss made me shred paperwork and write false entries in the ledger to hide what he'd taken. What's he looking at?
note: Theft Act s.17: false accounting, destroying, defacing, concealing or falsifying records made for an accounting purpose, up to seven years.

question: If the wrongdoing was done by a limited company, can they go after the managing director as an individual too?
note: Theft Act s.18: officers of a body corporate are personally liable where the company's offence was committed with their consent or connivance.

question: A director sent out a written update to shareholders that he knew was misleading. Is that a crime or just something for the regulator?
note: Theft Act s.19: false statements by company directors and officers intended to deceive members or creditors, up to seven years.

question: My uncle burnt my grandmother's will so the house would come to him. What offence is that?
note: Theft Act s.20: dishonestly destroying, defacing or concealing a will, valuable security or court or government document, up to seven years.

question: Someone is demanding money off me and says he'll send photos to my family if I don't pay. What offence is he committing?
note: Theft Act s.21: blackmail, an unwarranted demand with menaces made with a view to gain or to cause loss, up to fourteen years.

question: I bought a phone off a bloke in the pub for forty quid and I had a fair idea where it came from. How much trouble am I in?
note: Theft Act s.22: handling stolen goods knowing or believing them to be stolen, carrying up to fourteen years.

question: Can I put a card in the shop window offering cash for my bike back with no questions asked?
note: Theft Act s.23: advertising a reward for the return of stolen or lost goods using no questions asked wording, punishable by a fine.

question: The watch was nicked in Spain before it got over here. Does it count as stolen once it's in this country?
note: Theft Act s.24: scope of the stolen goods provisions, covering thefts abroad, proceeds of the original goods, and when goods stop being stolen.

question: A big sum landed in my bank account that clearly wasn't meant for me and I just sat on it. Am I in bother?
note: Theft Act s.24A: dishonestly failing to take reasonable steps to cancel a wrongful credit to an account, up to ten years.

question: Police stopped my cousin at two in the morning miles from home with bolt cutters and gloves in his bag. Can they do him for that on its own?
note: Theft Act s.25: going equipped, having an article with you away from home for use in a burglary or theft, up to three years.

question: Can the police get a magistrate to sign off on turning my house over looking for nicked gear?
note: Theft Act s.26: warrants to search for and seize stolen goods on information on oath before a justice of the peace.

question: Will the jury get told about my past convictions if I'm on trial for taking in dodgy gear?
note: Theft Act s.27: evidence and procedure on handling charges, including admitting earlier dealings with stolen goods and convictions in the past five years.

question: My husband emptied my savings account behind my back. Can he even be prosecuted for that while we're still married?
note: Theft Act s.30: applies the Act between spouses and civil partners, with prosecution generally needing the consent of the DPP.

question: He's been convicted over the painting he took off me. Does that conviction by itself put the ownership back in my name?
note: Theft Act s.31: effect on civil proceedings, self-incrimination in property proceedings, and title not being affected by the conviction alone.

question: My grandad talks about people being charged with larceny. Is that still a thing you can be charged with?
note: Theft Act s.32: abolishes the old common law offences including larceny, receiving and extortion, and how references to them are read now.

question: When the law talks about someone coming out ahead from what they did, does hanging onto something you already had count as coming out ahead?
note: Theft Act s.34: interpretation, defining gain and loss to include keeping what you have and not getting what you might get, and defining goods.

question: Can this law be used against somebody for something they did back in 1967?
note: Theft Act s.35: commencement on 1 January 1969 and effect only on offences wholly or partly committed on or after that date.

question: Does any of this apply if the whole thing happened up in Scotland?
note: Theft Act s.36: short title and extent, the Act not extending to Scotland or Northern Ireland apart from specified amendments and repeals.
